notes: main_tables.Rmd line 244: feols(log(IT + 1) ~ IBBEA | st_unit + st_year, data = main_df, cluster = 'state'). y = log(IT + 1) precomputed in the prepared CSV (so y_sd_regsample is the SD of the transformed outcome). Firm-year panel 1990-2005 (main_df, 6,308 rows, 722 st_units, 44 states). IBBEA = 1[year > year(plcyDate)], plcyDate constant within st_unit; g_year = year(plcyDate) + 1; verified IBBEA == 1[year >= g_year] on every row; no switch-offs. Cohorts (first treated year): 1996 (298 units), 1997 (142), 1998 (239), 2000 (42), 2002 (1); no never-treated units, so from 2001 on every observation is treated and comparisons rely on not-yet-treated units in 1996-2000 (only 1 untreated firm-year in 2000). st_year = block x year where block (recovered as the 11 connected components of the st_unit-st_year graph, stored as block_f) is a time-invariant firm grouping; passed as xt_vars so the FE are st_unit + year + year^block_f, numerically identical to st_unit + st_year. Data quirk: 6 firms that exit before their state's deregulation (never treated in sample, 21 firm-years) are duplicated once per block under distinct st_unit ids (66 st_units, 231 rows); kept as in the authors' regression. Prepared sample drops the 29 singleton observations (22 st_unit singletons, 7 block-year singletons) that the installed fixest removes anyway; coefficient unchanged (0.06092712), SE 0.02202 vs 0.02203 with singletons kept, N 6,279 vs the authors' 6,308. Author's preferred inventory-turnover estimate is probably Column 2 (controls + treat_customer, ineligible); the abstract's '6% faster inventory turnover' matches both columns. No article text in the project.
